Water solutions

Connecting water needs with workable solutions

Water opportunities begin with a specific need: reliable supply, better treatment, more efficient use, reuse or improved management of wastewater.

A promising technology is one part of the answer. It must also suit local conditions, operating capabilities, customer requirements and project economics.

We see scope to explore how Japanese and Indian businesses could bring technologies, market knowledge and delivery capabilities together around clearly defined needs.

Questions worth exploring

  • Whose water problem are we trying to solve, and what would a useful improvement look like?
  • How well does the proposed solution fit the site, customer and operating conditions?
  • Which technology, implementation and operating partners are needed?
  • What should a pilot establish before the parties consider a wider commitment?

Where SetuHashi could contribute

  • Define the opportunity

    Clarify the customer need, assess commercial potential and identify the requirements a solution must meet.

  • Develop the collaboration

    Bring prospective customers, technology businesses and delivery partners into discussions about fit, responsibilities and commercial arrangements.

  • Plan the path forward

    Help structure a pilot or phased approach, establish decision criteria and coordinate the business work needed to progress.

A practical starting point

A focused assessment of one customer need or application, followed by a partner discussion or pilot proposal where the opportunity warrants it.

Technical design, performance validation and applicable approvals would be addressed with the relevant qualified participants.
